arxiv-2206-14310.title: Stellar prospects for FRB gravitational lensing
arxiv-2206-14310.creator: Liam Connor, Vikram Ravi
arxiv-2206-14310.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Liam Connor, Vikram Ravi. Gravitational lensing of fast radio bursts (FRBs) offers an exciting avenue for several cosmological applications. However, it is not yet clear how many such events future surveys will detect nor how to optimally find them. We use the known properties of FRBs to forecast detection rates of gravitational lensing on delay timescales from microseconds to years, corresponding to lens masses spanning fifteen orders of magnitude.

arxiv-2207-00620.title: Multifamily Malware Models
arxiv-2207-00620.creator: Samanvitha Basole Fabio Di Troia Mark Stamp
arxiv-2207-00620.description: Abstract When training a machine learning model, there is likely to be a tradeoff between accuracy and the diversity of the dataset. Previous research has shown that if we train a model to detect one specific malware family, we generally obtain stronger results as compared to a case where we train a single model on multiple diverse families.

arxiv-2208-06470.title: A Concise History of the Black-body Radiation Problem
arxiv-2208-06470.creator: Himanshu Mavani and Navinder Singh
arxiv-2208-06470.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Himanshu Mavani and Navinder Singh. The way the topic of black-body radiation is presented in standard textbooks (i.e. from Rayleigh-Jeans to Max Planck) does not follow the actual historical timeline of the understanding of the black-body radiation problem. Authors believe that a presentation which follows an actual timeline of the ideas (although not a logical presentation of the field) would be of interest not only from the history of science perspective but also from a pedagogical perspective.

arxiv-2210-11749.title: Embedding dimensions of matrices whose entries are indefinite distances in the pseudo-Euclidean space
arxiv-2210-11749.creator: Hiroshi Nozaki, Masashi Shinohara, Sho Suda
arxiv-2210-11749.description: Abstract A finite set of the Euclidean space is called an s s -distance set provided the number of Euclidean distances in the set is s s . Determining the largest possible s s -distance set for the Euclidean space of a given dimension is challenging.

arxiv-2212-11981.description: Abstract We consider the extremal problem of interpolation of convex scattered data in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} by smooth edge convex curve networks with minimal L p L_{p} -norm of the second derivative for 1 < p ≤ ∞ 1<p\leq\infty . arxiv-2303-03655.title: Extended Lagrangian Born-Oppenheimer Molecular Dynamics with DFT+U
arxiv-2303-03655.creator: Yu Zhang, Marc J. Cawkwell, Christian F.A. Negre, Oscar Grånäs, Anders M. N. Niklasson
arxiv-2303-03655.description: Abstract Extended Lagrangian Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics (XL-BOMD) [Phys. Rev. Lett. vol. 100, 123004 (2008)] is combined with Kohn-Sham density functional theory (DFT) using a DFT+U correction based on the Hubbard model. This combined XL-BOMD and DFT+U approach allows efficient Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics simulations with orbital-dependent corrections beyond regular Kohn-Sham density functional theory.

arxiv-2303-13236.title: The lifespan estimates of radially symmetric solutions to systems of nonlinear wave equations in even space dimensions
arxiv-2303-13236.creator: Yuki Kurokawa
arxiv-2303-13236.description: Abstract The optimal lifespan estimates of a solution to weakly coupled systems of wave equations have been investigated by many works, except for the lower bound in even space dimensions. Our aim is to prove the open part under the assumption of radial symmetry on the solution.

arxiv-2409-05371.title: Gravitational lensing and shadows from thin-disks in Loop Quantum Gravity self-dual black holes
arxiv-2409-05371.creator: David J. Patiño Pomares, Diego Rubiera-Garcia
arxiv-2409-05371.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by David J. Patiño Pomares, Diego Rubiera-Garcia. We analyze gravitational lensing and their cast images from thin-disks in shadow observations of a family of spherically symmetric black hole solutions previously derived within the framework of Loop Quantum Gravity. Such black holes depend on two parameters (besides the mass of the black hole itself), P P and a 0 a_{0} , the latter imbuing the configurations with an interior wormhole structure.

arxiv-2507-13245.creator: Astghik Saharyan 1, Eloi Descamps 1, Arne Keller 1,2, Pérola Milman 1
arxiv-2507-13245.description: Abstract Quantum optics and atomic systems are prominent platforms for exploiting quantum-enhanced precision in parameter estimation. However, not only are quantum optical and atomic systems often treated separately, but even within quantum optics, identifying optimal probes (quantum states) and evolutions (parameter-dependent dynamics) typically relies on case-by-case analyses.

pmc-11721417.creator: Emily J. Baker, Gemma Allcott, Antonia Molloy, Jonathan A. G. Cox
pmc-11721417.description: Mycobacterium abscessus complex (MABSC) comprises a group of environmental microorganisms, which are a concerning cause of opportunistic respiratory infections in patients with cystic fibrosis or bronchiectasis. Only 45.6% of MABSC treatments are successful, and therefore this is a need to discover new antimicrobials that can treat these pathogens.

pmc-12379257.title: Soft porous metamaterials using inflation-induced buckling for smart actuation
pmc-12379257.creator: Kieran Barvenik, Michael Bonthron, Anthony Jones, Eleonora Tubaldi
pmc-12379257.description: Cellular metamaterials represent unique platforms to manipulate structure–property relationships and enhance mechanical responses. While their unconventional behaviors have traditionally been obtained via pattern-transformations under compressive loading or deflation, we theoretically investigate and experimentally realize a new class of soft, porous metamaterials that undergo buckling instability upon inflation, unlocking superior programming and sequencing capabilities for soft intelligent machines.

pmc-12707069.title: Dramatic biases in terrestrial nitrogen fixation in Earth System Models revealed by natural isotope signatures
pmc-12707069.creator: Maoyuan Feng, Shushi Peng, Philippe Ciais, Daniel S Goll, Benjamin Z Houlton, Ying-Ping Wang, Yilong Wang, Pan Liu, Joshua B Fisher, Pierre Regnier
pmc-12707069.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Biological nitrogen fixation (BNF) is the primary input of new reactive nitrogen to natural terrestrial ecosystems. However, this flux is poorly constrained due to its unclear drivers and associated control mechanisms. Here, we extend the existing theory of nitrogen (N) isotope mass balance to estimate BNF rates and then use a Bayesian approach to constrain the BNF rates in natural terrestrial ecosystems by using measurements of natural N-isotope ratios (δ15N) in plants (δP) and soil (δS).

pmc-13172880.title: 352 Macrophage regulation of inflammation in type 2 diabetes
pmc-13172880.creator: Tanvi Banota, Valerie Horsley, Kathryn Miller-Jensen
pmc-13172880.description: Objectives/Goals: Type 2 diabetes is a metabolic disease characterized by non-resolving inflammation.
